- All numeric fields are integers and accuracy/evasion use basis points (`accuracyBP` / `evadeBP`).

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## Summary

Addresses four pieces of professor feedback on the Q2 research report (`report/q2-report.tex`) **and computes the normalized error metric end-to-end** using the full 43 GB telemetry data.

1. **Normalized error metric (computed)** — Replaces the binary threshold scoring (τ_j) with a normalized error metric: Δ_j(D,D̃) / |Δ_j(D₁,D₂)|, where D₁,D₂ are random halves of the real dataset. The metric is now **fully computed**: `scripts/compute_normalized_error.py` splits 1M GUIDs 50/50 (seed 42), filters all 19 reporting tables, runs the 21-query benchmark on each half via DuckDB, and normalizes each method's errors by the baseline variation. Metrics where the baseline variation is below 10⁻⁸ (i.e., the two halves produce identical results) are excluded since they offer no natural variation to normalize against. Results are reported in two new LaTeX tables (per-method summary + per-query breakdown across 20 normalizable queries). Key finding: per-table DP-SGD achieves best median normalized error (2.72×), followed by PE (6.92×), MST (10.96×), wide-table (12.88×).

2. **Training curves** — Adds a training dynamics subsection with TikZ figures showing training loss (real data from `dp_vae_checkpoint.pt`: 23.76→17.31 over 20 epochs) and cumulative epsilon budget (1.64→3.996).

3. **PE prompt construction example** — Adds a new subsection with: the system instruction, a condensed prompt figure (via `tcolorbox`) showing schema layout with categorical pick-lists and numeric groups, a dummy record example showing the sparsity pattern (verified per-column rates from notebook output), and discussion of distributional prior divergence.

4. **MST baseline expansion** — Expands the 3-phase MST description with: exponential mechanism details for marginal selection, budget splitting for noisy measurement, Private-PGM fitting, discretization strategy (20 quantile bins + zero bin), SmartNoise v1.0.6 instantiation specifics, and per-table composition details.

Also adds `tcolorbox` LaTeX package and two new bibliography entries (McSherry & Talwar 2007, McKenna et al. 2019).

### Updates since last revision

- Fixed hardcoded `Section~2.3.1` → `Section~\ref{sec:normalized-error}` with proper `\label`
- Fixed incorrect `Section~\ref{fig:sensitivity}` → `Figure~\ref{fig:sensitivity}`
- Replaced placeholder training loss values with real data from checkpoint (23.76→17.31)
- Corrected PE sparsity percentages from placeholder to real per-column rates
- Computed normalized error metric end-to-end with `scripts/compute_normalized_error.py`
- Added Table~\ref{tab:normalized-error} (per-method summary) and Table~\ref{tab:normalized-error-per-query} (20-query breakdown) to report
- Updated conclusion section to highlight normalized error ranking
- Fixed Devin Review issues: duplicate `system_network_consumption`, ServerExpl row bolding, zero-baseline exclusion policy
- Re-ran experiment with corrected formula: updated median normalized errors are per-table 2.72×, PE 6.92×, MST 10.96×, wide-table 12.88×
- Formally documented the zero-baseline exclusion policy in Section 2.3.1: updated Equation 6 to remove η stabilizer term and explained why metrics with |Δ_j(D₁,D₂)| = 0 are excluded
- **Post-audit fixes**: Corrected XeonNet row bolding (PE is best at 5.1, not per-table at 6.5); fixed DisplayDurations value (13.7 not 13.8); corrected exclusion count from 18/281 to 18/282; updated per-table <5× count from 7 to 10 of 20 queries; fixed stale code comment in script
- **Codename consistency fix**: Fixed all 17 query codenames in the normalized error table (Table 8) that didn't match the official codenames defined in Table 2 (e.g., XeonNet→XeonGeo, BrowserCountry→BrowserRank, ServerExpl→NetAsymAgg, OnOffMods→SleepPivot, etc.). Also corrected query type labels to match Table 2's categories (Agg+Join→Agg, Top-k→Top-$k$, Geo/Demo→Geo, etc.) and updated all prose references that used the old ad-hoc names.
- **Code quality improvements** (latest): Wrapped DuckDB connection in try/finally for proper cleanup on exceptions; fixed step numbering mismatch between comments (1-8) and print statements (1-9) to both use steps 1-10; renamed d1_df/d2_df to d1_guid_df/d2_guid_df to avoid variable shadowing when reading CSVs later.
- LaTeX compiles cleanly: 43 pages, all cross-references resolve

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **Verify per-query normalized error table values match CSV output** — The table at lines 948-967 contains hand-transcribed values from `data/results/normalized_error/normalized_error_per_query_method.csv`. Spot-check 5-10 rows against the CSV to catch any remaining transcription errors. Five errors were already caught and fixed (XeonNet bolding, DisplayDurations 13.7, etc.), but others may remain.
- [ ] **Verify query codename mapping is correct** — 17 of 20 codenames were renamed to match Table 2. Cross-check the mapping against Table 2 (lines 188-212) to verify no mistakes were made (e.g., confirm XeonGeo→XeonNet was indeed the intended fix, not a different query).
- [ ] **Verify try/finally refactor didn't introduce logic errors** — The main() function in `compute_normalized_error.py` was re-indented to add try/finally. Visually inspect the indentation changes (lines 246-391) to ensure no code blocks were accidentally de-indented or mis-indented.
- [ ] **Verify "10 of 20 queries below 5×" claim** — Report states per-table achieves normalized errors <5× on 10 of 20 queries (lines 971, 1358). Cross-check against the per-query CSV to confirm the count is accurate (this was updated from 7 to 10 after the audit).
- [ ] **LaTeX compilation** — Independently compile with `xelatex q2-report.tex && bibtex q2-report && xelatex q2-report.tex && xelatex q2-report.tex` to verify all packages are available and cross-references resolve.

**Suggested test plan:** Compile LaTeX end-to-end. Review the normalized error table (Table 8, page ~38) and verify codenames match Table 2 exactly. Spot-check 10-15 values against the CSV output (`data/results/normalized_error/normalized_error_per_query_method.csv`). Search the document for any remaining instances of old codenames (XeonNet, OnOffMods, etc.). Verify the try/finally refactor in `compute_normalized_error.py` didn't introduce any logical errors by reviewing the indentation diff.

### Notes

This PR is **documentation + data analysis** (LaTeX + Python script). The normalized error computation script is committed, but output CSVs are gitignored since they require the full 43 GB telemetry data to reproduce. The LaTeX tables contain the computed values.

The zero-baseline exclusion policy means 18 metrics (out of 282 total metric measurements across all queries/methods) were dropped because they had no natural variation to normalize against. This primarily affected Jaccard group-coverage metrics where D₁ and D₂ produced identical group key sets. As a result, the per-query normalized error table lists 20 of 21 queries (WaitStateRank is omitted because all of its metrics had zero baseline variation).

The methodology section explains why exclusion is preferred over eta-stabilization: eta-stabilized ratios (e.g., `0.5 / 10⁻⁸ = 5×10⁷`) produce astronomically large values that dominate summary statistics without conveying meaningful synthesis quality information.

**Devin Review findings (latest commit `6aec370`):** 0 bugs, 3 informational flags (20/21 queries in table is expected due to zero-baseline exclusion; type annotation for split_guids could be more precise but has no runtime impact; SQL regex adaptation assumes `reporting.` prefix which works correctly for all 19 query files). All previous flags have been resolved.

body:
Implements a complete three-tier architecture on AWS using Terraform for a personal Google Drive clone with S3-backed file storage.

## Architecture

- **T1 (Database)**: PostgreSQL RDS in private subnets (disabled by default for cost)
- **T2 (Application)**: Flask API on EC2 ASG with S3 file operations
- **T3 (Presentation)**: Node.js Express web UI behind ALB
- **Storage**: S3 bucket with versioning, AES-256 encryption, lifecycle policies

## Changes

### Terraform (`terraform/`)
- Added S3 bucket with versioning, encryption, CORS, lifecycle policies
- Added IAM policy for S3 access attached to EC2 instance role
- Added `app_tier_url`, `environment`, `db_name` variables
- Updated outputs with S3 bucket info and architecture summary

### App Tier (`app-tier/`)
- Full REST API: upload, download, delete, list files, presigned URLs, storage stats
- S3 integration via boto3

### Web Tier (`web-tier/`)
- Google Drive-like UI with drag-and-drop uploads
- File browser with type icons, search, storage usage display
- API proxy to app tier

## API Endpoints

```
POST   /files/upload           # Upload file to S3
GET    /files                  # List files
GET    /files/download/:id     # Download file
DELETE /files/:id              # Delete file
GET    /files/:id/presigned    # Get presigned URL
GET    /storage/stats          # Storage statistics
```

## Security
- S3 public access blocked
- Server-side encryption (AES-256)
- multer updated to 2.1.1 (fixes DoS vulnerabilities)
- CodeQL: no alerts

body:
### Motivation

- Provide a standalone Zabbix plugin that ingests metrics from an external JSON API, persists them to NoSQL storage, and orchestrates Zabbix item updates with dynamic check intervals. 
- Offer a lightweight web UI and REST API for configuring services and dependencies and for visualizing impact chains. 
- Ship a minimal project scaffold with packaging, README, and automated tests to validate core flows.

### Description

- Introduce a new Python package `zbx_json_plugin` with modules for CLI (`cli.py`), runtime orchestration (`plugin.py`), JSON source client (`json_api.py`), Zabbix JSON-RPC client (`zabbix_api.py`), Mongo storage adapter (`storage.py`), state/UI models (`state.py`), UI server (`ui_server.py`), dependency graph logic (`dependencies.py`), metric grouping (`metrics.py`), interval tuning (`intervals.py`), and logging helpers (`logging_utils.py`).
- Implement `ZabbixJsonPlugin.run_once` to fetch payloads via `JsonApiClient`, group metrics with `MetricGroup`, persist to `MongoMetricStorage`, adjust check interval via `adjust_check_interval`, and update Zabbix items/events via `ZabbixApiClient`.
- Add a small single-file web UI served by `ui_server.py` exposing REST endpoints `GET /api/state`, `PUT /api/config`, `POST /api/services`, `POST /api/dependencies`, and `GET /api/impact/{service_id}`, backed by `StateStore` persistence.
- Add packaging and tooling files: `pyproject.toml`, `README.md`, `.gitignore`, and a console script entry `zbx-json-plugin`.

### Testing

- Added unit tests `tests/test_cli_logging.py`, `tests/test_plugin.py`, and `tests/test_ui_and_state.py` covering CLI parsing/logging, plugin success/error flows, metric grouping, dependency impact traversal, `StateStore` roundtrip, and the UI REST endpoints.

author: mtrossbach
body:
fix(apple): reorder CoreLogic property initializers to prevent EXC_BAD_ACCESS on iOS

  Move `workSchedulerProvider` and `audioNormalizedLoudnessBuilder` before
  `globalCallManager` to fix a crash on iOS startup.

  Root cause:
  Kotlin property initializers run strictly in declaration order. The previous order was:

      globalCallManager    = GlobalCallManager(getGlobalScope(), ...)  // line 100
      workSchedulerProvider = WorkSchedulerProviderImpl()               // line 101

  `GlobalCallManager(getGlobalScope(), ...)` triggers the lazy initialization
  of `globalKaliumScope` in the parent class `CoreLogicCommon`. That lazy
  block constructs `GlobalKaliumScope(...)`, which in its own initializer
  immediately (non-lazily) calls:

      workSchedulerProvider.globalWorkScheduler(this)

  At this point, `workSchedulerProvider`'s initializer on line 101 has not yet
  run. In Kotlin/Native the backing field is therefore still zero-initialized
  (`null` at the native memory level). Dispatching a method call on a null
  pointer results in EXC_BAD_ACCESS (code=1, address=0x0).

  In Kotlin/JVM the same code would throw a NullPointerException at runtime,
  making the bug obvious. In Kotlin/Native the call site is compiled to a
  direct native function dispatch with no null check, so the crash manifests
  as a hard memory fault rather than an exception — and the stack trace points
  into `globalWorkScheduler`, not to the uninitialized property, which obscures
  the real cause.

allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)

Currently only one GitHub repo/token pair can be configured per JWT cookie. This adds support for multiple repositories in the same JWT, with a sidebar dropdown to switch between them, add new ones, or disconnect individual repos.

## JWT structure change

The cookie payload changes from a flat `GitHubConfig` object to a store:

```typescript
// Before
{ token, owner, repo, branch }

// After
{ configs: GitHubConfig[], activeIndex: number }
```

Old single-config JWTs are auto-migrated on first read — no logout required.

## Server changes

- **`server/utils/jwt.ts`** — New types (`GitHubConfig`, `GitHubConfigStore`) exported publicly. Added `getGitHubConfigStoreFromRequest`, `setGitHubConfigStore`, `clearGitHubConfigCookie`. `getGitHubConfigFromRequest` preserved for backward compat (returns active config).
- **`config.post.ts`** — Appends to the configs array (or updates in-place by `owner+repo`) instead of overwriting the cookie.
- **`config.get.ts`** — Now returns `repos[]` (tokens excluded) and `activeIndex` alongside the existing `config` field.
- **`switch.post.ts`** *(new)* — `POST /api/github/switch` — updates `activeIndex` in the JWT.
- **`disconnect.post.ts`** *(new)* — `POST /api/github/disconnect` — removes a config by index; clears cookie entirely when the last repo is removed.

## UI changes

- **`Sidebar.vue`** — Repo name replaced with a dropdown button. Shows all connected repos (active marked with ✓), per-row disconnect button on hover, and a "Connect another repository" entry at the bottom. Click-outside closes it.
- **`pages/index.vue`** — Tracks `githubRepos[]` and `githubActiveRepoIndex`. Handles `switch-repo` (calls switch endpoint, re-syncs files), `add-repo` (opens config modal), and `disconnect-repo` (calls disconnect endpoint, shows login modal if no repos remain).

body: The implementations of the cel algorithm (for complete elliptic integrals) in special_cel.py have an errtol (error tolerance) that determines the number of iterations that these routines perform, resulting in a relative accuracy of the result of 10^-D (i.e., D digits) for an errtol = 10^(-D/2), according to the paper by Bulirsch. The value of errtol is hardcoded, and different in magpylib's `cel` vs. `cel_iter` implementations: 10^-6 in the former (as in the Bulirsch and Derby papers, and their analog in M. Ortner's article) vs. 10^-8 in cel_iter (and celx and celxx in M. Ortner's article). This PR attempts to harmonize these by introducing a common `_errtol = 1e-8`, which would seem appropriate (approximately equal to the square root of machine epsilon for a float64). This improves the convergence of `cel()`, as shown in this graph: Going from right to left, the steps correspond to the increasing number of iterations and concomitant improvement in convergence of `cel()` using either the standard float64 or more precise quad datatype; it agrees with Bulirsch expectations for the relative accuracy. Going from 10^-6 to 10^-8 gives you 2 extra digits accuracy at the cost of an extra iteration, apparently. For definiteness: the graph is generated as follows: ``` import numpy_quaddtype as npq import magpylib as magpy import matplotlib import matplotlib.pyplot as plt e = np.linspace(-16, -1, 50) kc = 0.9 rslt = [] qrslt = [] for ee in e: magpy._src.fields.special_cel._errtol = 10**ee c = magpy._src.fields.special_cel._cel0(kc, 1., 1., 0.) rslt.append(c) cq = magpy._src.fields.special_cel._cel0(np.array(kc, dtype=npq.QuadPrecDType()), 1., 1., 0.) qrslt.append(cq) plt.figure() plt.semilogy(e, np.abs(np.array(rslt)-qrslt[0])) plt.semilogy(e, np.abs(np.array(qrslt)-qrslt[0])) plt.xlabel('errtol') plt.ylabel('abs(cel(errtol)-cel(1e-16))') plt.legend(['double, i.e., float64', 'quad']) ``` The proposed PR also changes the convergence criterion in cel_iter0/v to match that in the Ortner article and Bulirsch paper (it was subtly different, somehow). As an alternative to `_errtol = 1e-8`, we could set _errtol to `np.sqrt(np.finfo(x.dtype))`, and get rid of the hard-coded constant completely. Please advise.

💡 **What:** 
Replaced the synchronous `requests.get` call inside the `validate_key_with_soma` auth verification flow with a pooled, asynchronous `httpx.AsyncClient`. Updated the `verify_api_key` FastAPI dependency to be `async def`. Added initialization logic inside the application's `lifespan` context manager to instantiate and reuse a global `httpx.AsyncClient` safely.

🎯 **Why:** 
The previous implementation used blocking I/O (`requests.get`) inside a FastAPI dependency. Even though FastAPI runs synchronous dependencies in a background thread pool, a burst of concurrent requests to endpoints validating against the remote auth service would quickly exhaust the worker threads, crippling the application's throughput and increasing latency exponentially across all endpoints.

📊 **Measured Improvement:** 
I developed a benchmarking suite simulating multiple concurrent requests with a remote network delay (500ms simulated latency):
*   **Baseline (Sync requests):** ~68.7 req/s
*   **Optimized (Async httpx):** ~87.5 req/s

This optimization provides a **1.27x throughput improvement** under high concurrency and drastically reduces the risk of threadpool starvation during latency spikes from the external Soma auth service.

body:
## About The Pull Request

Originally I wanted to blame this on #13722 because these issues only arose after it was merged, but after looking at the code before it was merged, it really makes no sense how it was even working in the first place.

Anyways, several `SSpolling.whatever_poll()` calls expect one `/mob` candidate to be returned, however, none of them had `amount_to_pick` set to `1`. This meant a `/list` was always returned and this broke every `SSpolling` request that expected a `/mob` type to be returned. The simple solution was to set `amount_to_pick` to `1` for all relevant cases.

Additionally, I always hated the following pattern:
```dm
var/datum/poll_config/config = new()
config.question = "Do you wish to be considered for this role?"
config.poll_time = 30 SECONDS
```

So, I gave poll configs constructors and it now looks like:
```dm
var/datum/poll_config/config = new(
    question = "Do you wish to be considered for this role?",
    poll_time = 30 SECONDS,
)
```

The following python script was used to convert all poll configs to use constructors. There was some weirdness in `antag_spawner.dm` and `cult_comms.dm` which required manual correction.

<details>
<summary>Script</summary>

```py
import re
from pathlib import Path

root_dir = Path("PATH_TO_DIRECTORY")

pattern = re.compile(
    r'^([ \t]*)var/datum/poll_config/config\s*=\s*new\(\)\s*\n((?:[ \t]*config\.\w+\s*=\s*.*\n)+)',
    re.MULTILINE
)

def transform(match):
    base_indent = match.group(1)
    assignments = match.group(2)

    arg_indent = base_indent + "\t"

    args = []
    for line in assignments.splitlines():
        m = re.match(r'\s*config\.(\w+)\s*=\s*(.*)', line)
        if m:
            key = m.group(1)
            value = m.group(2).rstrip()
            args.append(f"{arg_indent}{key} = {value},")

    args_block = "\n".join(args)

    return f"{base_indent}var/datum/poll_config/config = new(\n{args_block}\n{base_indent})\n"

for file in root_dir.rglob("*.dm"):
    text = file.read_text(encoding="utf-8")

    new_text, count = pattern.subn(transform, text)

    if count:
        file.write_text(new_text, encoding="utf-8")
        print(f"Updated {file} ({count} replacements)")
```

</details>

## Summary

Fixes #4635

On Windows, files inside `.git/objects/` are marked read-only by default. When `adk deploy` cleans up the temporary directory in its `finally` block, `shutil.rmtree()` raises `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access denied` on these files, causing the CLI to crash even after a successful deployment.

This PR introduces a `_robust_rmtree()` helper that passes an error handler to `shutil.rmtree`. On Windows, the handler clears the read-only bit (`os.chmod(path, stat.S_IWRITE)`) and retries the deletion. On non-Windows platforms, `shutil.rmtree` is called without any handler. The fix uses `onexc` for Python >= 3.12 and `onerror` for Python < 3.12 to avoid deprecation warnings.

All six `shutil.rmtree()` call sites in `cli_deploy.py` (`to_cloud_run`, `to_agent_engine`, `to_gke`) are updated.

  - `test_removes_directory_tree` -- verifies normal directory removal
  - `test_removes_readonly_files` -- verifies removal of trees containing read-only files
  - `test_on_rm_error_clears_readonly_and_retries` -- verifies the error handler chmod + retry logic

body:
## Description

Partially addresses #119 (Bug 2: custom `client_secret.json` ignored)

### Problem

`config_dir()` used `dirs::config_dir()` which resolves to different paths per OS:

| Platform | `dirs::config_dir()/gws/` | README says |
|----------|--------------------------|-------------|
| Linux | `~/.config/gws/` | `~/.config/gws/` (correct) |
| macOS | `~/Library/Application Support/gws/` | `~/.config/gws/` (wrong) |
| Windows | `%APPDATA%\gws\` | `~/.config/gws/` (wrong) |

Users on macOS/Windows who followed the README and placed `client_secret.json` at `~/.config/gws/` had their config silently ignored because the CLI was reading from a different OS-specific path.

### Solution

- Changed `config_dir()` to use `~/.config/gws/` on all platforms (via `dirs::home_dir()`)
- Added backward-compatible fallback: if `~/.config/gws/` doesn't exist but the legacy OS-specific path does, it uses the legacy path (existing users are not affected)
- Consolidated duplicated `dirs::config_dir()` calls in `auth.rs` and `discovery.rs` to use the central `config_dir()` helper

### Fallback logic

1. `~/.config/gws/` exists → use it (new installs, Linux users)
2. `dirs::config_dir()/gws/` exists → use it (existing macOS/Windows users)
3. Neither exists → use `~/.config/gws/` (will be created on first write)

On Linux, both paths are identical so there is no behavioral change.

**Dry Run Output:**
```

```

**Restart-safe state restoration and persistence:**

This is reflected in both the `README.md` and the implementation in `coordinator.py`, with new helpers for building, merging, and saving node snapshots. ### Motivation

- Provide a non-blocking way to validate live API requests/responses against the Django OpenAPI schema during Playwright e2e runs so CI can surface schema mismatches as artifacts. 
- Allow Playwright to opt-in to validation and aggregate findings across the test run for reporting without failing tests.

### Description

- Added a Django middleware `posthog.openapi_validation_middleware.OpenAPISchemaValidationMiddleware` that validates `/api/*` requests/responses using `openapi-core` when `OPENAPI_E2E_VALIDATION_ENABLED` is enabled and records a per-response header `X-PostHog-OpenAPI-Validation-Errors` with the finding count. 
- Exposed configuration flags in `posthog/settings/web.py`: `OPENAPI_E2E_VALIDATION_ENABLED`, `OPENAPI_E2E_VALIDATION_HEADER`, and `OPENAPI_E2E_VALIDATION_HEADER_VALUE` and registered the middleware in `MIDDLEWARE`. 
- Instrumented Playwright: added conditional header injection and a custom reporter in `playwright/playwright.config.ts` when `PLAYWRIGHT_OPENAPI_VALIDATE` is set, plus README docs describing how to enable validation during e2e runs. 
- Implemented Playwright-side utilities and reporter: `playwright/utils/openapi-validation.ts` collects per-response findings, `playwright/utils/playwright-test-core.ts` starts/stops the collector and attaches summaries to tests, and `playwright/reporters/openapi-validation-reporter.ts` aggregates per-test attachments into `openapi-validation-summary.json`. 
- Added dependency `openapi-core` to `pyproject.toml` and included a lightweight unit test `posthog/test/test_openapi_validation_middleware.py` covering middleware enable/disable and header behavior.

### Testing

- Ran the new unit test `TestOpenAPISchemaValidationMiddleware` which verifies middleware is disabled when the flag is off and that it reports a non-blocking aggregated error count when enabled, and the test passed. 
- Playwright e2e reporter and collector logic was added but not gated by additional automated Playwright test coverage in this change (reporter activation is conditional on `PLAYWRIGHT_OPENAPI_VALIDATE`).

body:
When I logged into lobsters my autofilled TOTP code from bitwarden was invalid. I've never had that happen before and I thought the [spec](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6238#section-6) had something to say about clock skew:

>  Because of possible clock drifts between a client and a validation
   server, we RECOMMEND that the validator be set with a specific limit
   to the number of time steps a prover can be "out of synch" before
   being rejected.
>
> This limit can be set both forward and backward from the calculated
   time step on receipt of the OTP value.  If the time step is
   30 seconds as recommended, and the validator is set to only accept
   two time steps backward, then the maximum elapsed time drift would be
   around 89 seconds, i.e., 29 seconds in the calculated time step and
   60 seconds for two backward time steps.
>
>   This would mean the validator could perform a validation against the
   current time and then two further validations for each backward step
   (for a total of 3 validations).  Upon successful validation, the
   validation server can record the detected clock drift for the token
   in terms of the number of time steps.  When a new OTP is received
   after this step, the validator can validate the OTP with the current
   timestamp adjusted with the recorded number of time-step clock drifts
   for the token.

ROTP supports checking for drift in [`ROTP::TOTP.verify`](https://www.rubydoc.info/github/mdp/rotp/main/ROTP/TOTP#verify-instance_method).

P.S. Thanks for the devcontainer configuration. It made getting a dev environment almost instant.

Renamed per-field option keys with `Fn` suffix to resolve the type conflict:

- `encrypt` → `encryptFn`
- `decrypt` → `decryptFn`
- `isEncrypted` → `isEncryptedFn`

Global encryption functions (`setEncryptionFunctions`, plugin options) are unchanged.
